title: Grateful Dead Live at Carousel Ballroom on 1968-02-14
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent two‑track soundboard capture of the legendary 2/14/68 Valentine’s Day show, highlighted by a monster New Potato→Spanish Jam and an all‑out Alligator‑Caution‑Feedback sequence.
ai_review.review: This SBD recording is surprisingly clear for 1968, with only a brief cut in the Alligator jam and occasional level quirks. Musically the concert is fire‑breathing – the second set reads like a single epic suite, featuring New Potato, Spanish Jam, Dark Star, The Eleven, Lovelight and an unforgettable Anthems‑of‑the‑Sun medley. Reviewers rave about the band’s raw energy, tight transitions and standout playing from every member.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 70 reviews, the vast majority are 5‑star with consistent praise for both performance and sound quality; only a handful of lower or mixed ratings exist.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Two‑track SBD is remarkably crisp with little hiss; occasional level issues (Jerry’s guitar/vocals low, overall volume a hair soft) and a ~1 min cut in the Alligator jam that many patch from Anthem of the Sun. A few dropouts/splurts are noted but do not detract from overall listenability.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth, almost suite‑like transitions – New Potato flows into Spanish Jam, the Anthems‑of‑the‑Sun sequence runs uninterrupted, and the second set builds a continuous wave of energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s ‘crunchy’ tone and soaring solos are repeatedly praised; some note his guitar is mixed low in places but overall his playing drives the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s “manic” bass lines and occasional vocal moments receive strong kudos; several reviewers call his improvisations after vocals a highlight.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir is described as a rhythm‑guitar monster with strong vocals for this era, adding solid texture to the jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ron "Pigpen" McKernan’s calliope organ dominates early tracks, providing the signature riff in Dark Star and fueling the psychedelic atmosphere.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann are lauded as a “symbiotic eight‑limbed rhythm machine,” laying down tight, grooving foundations throughout.
